- When sentiment is negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1.00), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 1–2% to avoid overfitting to sentiment.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 68.00 after 70+), model often fails to correct; adjust forecast to align with 30d moving average of prior 10 days.
- For 30d forecasts, if model consistently overpredicts by >2% over 3–5 prior days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 7 days unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history includes 2+ negative days in last 5, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate for bearish sentiment lag.
